title: the batch key is a client-supplied header, and `import_staging` has no tenancy column of its own
what_is_wrong: an untrusted request header is interpolated unvalidated into the key that `applyBatch` and `deleteMany` select on, and the staging table carries no `org_id` at all, so the `orgId-` prefix inside a text field is the only thing separating one org's staging rows from another's.

file: src/routes/import.ts — `const csv = await req.text(); if (csv.length > MAX_CSV_BYTES)`; sr
title: the size limit runs after the whole body is buffered, counts UTF-16 units rather than bytes, and no bound exists on row count or upsert fan-out
what_is_wrong: `await req.text()` has already materialised the entire request body in memory before the check runs, `String.length` counts UTF-16 code units so a constant named `MAX_CSV_BYTES` admits roughly three times that many bytes of multi-byte text, and nothing caps the number of parsed rows or batches the promotion writes.

title: a CSV whose header lacks an `email` column is accepted and reported as a successful import of nothing
what_is_wrong: when `indexOf` returns `-1` the code silently produces `email: ""` for every row instead of rejecting the input, and the first line is consumed as a header unconditionally, so a header-less CSV also loses its first data row.

file: test/import/parse.test.ts — the only test file in the diff; untested exports are `enterSys
title: every new export except `parseRows` ships with no test, including the audit control this change rewrites
what_is_wrong: the change adds and modifies a security control and its only consumer while the test diff touches nothing but the CSV parser, so the guard is exercised by no test at all and the parser's nine cases give the suite a green that reads as coverage.

file: docs/import.md — "The staging writes are the single exception ... the promotion step runs
title: the documentation and the context comment describe a bounded, authority-gated exception that the code does not implement
what_is_wrong: both claims are stronger than the implementation — the promotion step does not run audited (first finding), the staging writes are not the single exception, and "only system operations may call this" is a convention no mechanism enforces, so a control every reader will take for an enforceable boundary is in fact detect

title: `contextSnapshot` is exported, unused, and copies the suspension flag out of the context
what_is_wrong: nothing in the diff calls it, and the shallow copy it returns includes `skipAudit`, so a caller who later feeds a stored snapshot back through `runWithContext` would resurrect a suspension the original request had finished with.
